meta.title: Timing drive by engine: belt, chain or wet belt, and the belt change interval
meta.what: For the used cars most inspected in Finland in 2025, one entry per make, model and engine family: whether the camshafts are driven by a dry timing belt, a timing chain or a wet belt (a belt running in engine oil), and the belt change interval where a source gives one.
meta.method: Models chosen by 2025 inspection count in traficom-inspections.json (byModelAllYears, top 100; Tesla Model 3 has no timing drive). Engines were looked up on the web on the date above. Maker documents (owner's manuals, service schedules, VW/Audi/Skoda Self-Study Programmes, press kits) are primary; trade, press, parts-maker and workshop-data sources (ADAC, Haynes maintenance plans, Gates, NTN-SNR, febi, CompleteCar, auto motor und sport) are secondary and the entry says secondary: true. Forums, Q&A sites and Wikipedia were not used. ADAC's Autokatalog was also read page by page (camshaft drive and engine code per variant) to fill gaps and to cross-check: an ADAC engine code is used only when every ADAC page read for it gives the same drive and at least two pages do. Before writing the file, every quote was checked again against its source; entries whose quote could not be found again were dropped. A model year whose engines differ under the same ad name (a switch year, two engine families with one badge) is split or that name is left out for those years. The quotes, notes and the list of what was left out and why are in the evidence file.

conventions.id: Stable key of the entry; the evidence file is keyed by it.
conventions.make, model: Traficom's names, exactly as the keys in traficom-inspections.json (byModel, byModelAllYears).
conventions.years: [from, to] first-registration years (Traficom's käyttöönottovuosi), inclusive, within 2005-2022.
conventions.fuel: petrol | diesel | hybrid (petrol full hybrid) | plug-in hybrid | CNG. A 48 V mild hybrid is filed under its base fuel.
conventions.engine: displacementL; badges = how ads name the engine (match case-insensitively; a bare displacement such as "1.6" also counts); codes = engine family and engine codes from the sources (ADAC gives some as 3-letter prefixes).
conventions.drive: belt (dry timing belt) | chain | wet belt (belt in oil, e.g. PSA PureTech 1.0/1.2, Ford EcoBoost 1.0)
conventions.intervalKm, intervalYears: Belt change interval, whichever comes first, only where the cited source states it; absent otherwise and always absent for a chain. Most intervals are Haynes's general European schedule, which is labelled 'except Norway, Finland, Sweden' on many plans.
conventions.source: Id in meta.sources; it states the drive (and the interval if given).
conventions.secondary: true when the drive or the interval rests on a secondary source (not the car maker's own document).

sources.name: ADAC Autokatalog, technical data per model variant (Motorcode, Nockenwellensteuerung); the exact pages are listed per entry in the evidence file
